doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Original songs and the record business
title: 'DaVinci's Eyes': accordion, Don Sebesky's arrangement and Jessica's lyrics
summary: He explains the song's accordion sound, the arrangement by Don Sebesky, and the lyrics by Jessica Molaskey. The song was popular on their pandemic Facebook show.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It is indeed. It’s a beautiful song and I just was listening to it and I loved it when the accordion came in and I got this sense of your family history and Bucky talking about the accordion and all that. And so I just wanted to say nice going, and Jessica, I don’t know how this line came up to be but there’s the line that it sort of waits to get to, and then “What DaVinci would do with your eyes.”

That’s a great line. It’s a great song. And what happened was it’s based on well Dominick Cortese plays the accordion and he’s a family friend. And he’s the accordion player on, there’s a song called “Where’s the Orchestra” that ends the “Allentown” record, Billy Joel’s record. And it’s similar to that kind of thing. And I always loved that sound. And Don Sebesky wrote the arrangement for the cello and Ken Peplowski and Harry Allen and Dominick. Because Sebesky’s an old — was an old accordion player. And I sort of liked the idea that was that [scats and sings] what DaVinci would do, what DaVinci would do with your eyes. Molaskey’s written a lot of great lyrics and so we sneak them on the records and we don’t really know if anybody listens to them.
Well they do, at least I do.

Thank you. I’ll pass that along. That was one of the first songs we played on our FaceBook Thursday night show during the pandemic and everybody went crazy for “DaVinci’s Eyes” the first couple of weeks we played it so we kept looking at each other and going are they hearing the right stuff?
